1,140 of 1,140 unique sites (100%) in Zebra Finch are removed by the filter; 0 sites are retained.

Definition/calculation:
- A site = unique Pos (= "Chromosome_StartPosition"; identical to unique (Chromosome, StartPosition, EndPosition)) → 1,140 unique sites in ZF_AgeRelated_CpG_noMT_Final.csv (19,698 rows × 12 columns, one row per site×sample).
- Aggregation: per-site methylation = mean of MethylationPercentage across the samples present at that site (no missing values; no zero-coverage rows; rows-per-site 2–20, median 20).
- Filter (strict): a site is retained only if its value is <10% OR >90%; a site is removed if 10% ≤ value ≤ 90%. No site is exactly 10 or 90, so boundary handling does not change the count.
- Result: site mean methylation spans 40.02–59.99 (per-site pooled: 19.7–86.0); no site falls below 10% or above 90%, so all 1,140 sites are removed.

Sensitivity (explicitly kept separate, not the main answer): if a site were instead considered "extreme" when ANY sample row is <10% or >90% (row-level), then 849 sites would be removed and 291 retained. Under the approved site-level aggregation (mean; confirmed identical for median and pooled sums), the answer is 1,140 removed.

Assumptions: (1) per-site aggregation via mean across samples (primary; median/pooled give the same result); (2) strict thresholds, removed iff 10% ≤ value ≤ 90%; (3) only the ZF file is used ("in Zebra Finch"); JD and Chromosome_Length files are irrelevant to this question; (4) no NaN/zero-coverage handling needed (0 missing, 0 Coverage==0 rows).
